Others, again, pass so rapidly from place to place, and are so general in their description, the reader gets but very imperfect ideas from reading them. These extremes the writer has endeavoured to avoid.

arxiv-2008-06303.title: Search for new phenomena in top quark interactions
arxiv-2008-06303.creator: K. Skovpen (on behalf of the ATLAS and CMS Collaborations)
arxiv-2008-06303.description: Abstract The study of the processes with the production of top quarks represents a unique possibility to test the standard model (SM) predictions and probe the new physics effects. Potential deviations from the SM expectations are parametrized within the framework of the Effective Field Theory (EFT). The latest EFT results from ATLAS and CMS experiments are presented.

arxiv-2109-08936.title: Charged Lepton EDM with Extra Yukawa Couplings
arxiv-2109-08936.creator: Wei-Shu Hou, Girish Kumar and Sven Teunissen
arxiv-2109-08936.description: Abstract In a two Higgs doublet model with extra Yukawa couplings, we assess the new physics contributions to charged lepton electric dipole moment. We focus especially on muon (and tau) EDM where in the coming decade several experiments — Muon g-2, J-PARC and PSI (and Belle II) — will push sensitivities down by several orders of magnitude.

arxiv-2402-08471.title: Holographic Turbulence From a Random Gravitational Potential
arxiv-2402-08471.creator: Yaron Oz, a , Sebastian Waeber b , Amos Yarom b
arxiv-2402-08471.description: Abstract We study the turbulent dynamics of a relativistic ( 2 + 1 ) (2+1) -dimensional fluid placed in a stochastic gravitational potential. We demonstrate that the dynamics of the fluid can be obtained using a dual holographic description realized by an asymptotically Anti-de Sitter black brane driven by a random boundary metric.

arxiv-2405-17397.title: Occlusion Handling in 3D Human Pose Estimation with Perturbed Positional Encoding
arxiv-2405-17397.creator: Niloofar Azizi, Mohsen Fayyaz, Horst Bischof
arxiv-2405-17397.description: Abstract Understanding human behavior fundamentally relies on accurate 3D human pose estimation. Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have recently shown promising advancements, delivering state-of-the-art performance with rather lightweight architectures. In the context of graph-structured data, leveraging the eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian matrix for positional encoding is effective.

arxiv-2408-12306.title: Pulse characterization at the single-photon level through chronocyclic Q Q -function measurements
arxiv-2408-12306.creator: Abhinandan Bhattacharjee, 1,* Patrick Folge, 1 Laura Serino, 1 Jaroslav Řeháček, 2 Zdeněk Hradil, 2 Christine Silberhorn, 1 and Benjamin Brecht 1
arxiv-2408-12306.description: Abstract The characterization of the complex spectral amplitude that is, the spectrum and spectral phase, of single-photon-level light fields is a crucial capability for modern photonic quantum technologies. Since established pulse characterisation techniques are not applicable at low intensities, alternative approaches are required.

arxiv-2508-06319.title: Towards Balanced Behavior Cloning from Imbalanced Datasets Journal: Autonomous Robots
arxiv-2508-06319.creator: Sagar Parekh, Heramb Nemlekar, and Dylan P. Losey
arxiv-2508-06319.description: Abstract Robots should be able to learn complex behaviors from human demonstrations. In practice, these human-provided datasets are inevitably imbalanced : i.e., the human demonstrates some subtasks more frequently than others. State-of-the-art methods default to treating each element of the human’s dataset as equally important.

arxiv-2510-20806.title: Testing the AGN Paradigm, Part I: a generic SED for Seyfert 1 galaxies.
arxiv-2510-20806.creator: Paulina Alejandra Roco-Avilez, Roger Coziol, Juan Pablo Torres-Papaqui, Karla Alejandra Cutiva-Alvarez, María Fernanda La Rotta-Wilches, César David Aguirre-Gutiérrez, Angélica Gabriela Sandoval-Esparza
arxiv-2510-20806.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Paulina Alejandra Roco-Avilez, Roger Coziol, Juan Pablo Torres-Papaqui, Karla Alejandra Cutiva-Alvarez, María Fernanda La Rotta-Wilches, César David Aguirre-Gutiérrez, Angélica Gabriela Sandoval-Esparza. This article presents the first part of a study aimed at testing the unification paradigm for AGN (UPAGN) using the SED reconstruction code X-CIGALE.

pmc-11637722.title: PembroWM: A phase II trial to investigate the safety and efficacy of rituximab and pembrolizumab in relapsed/refractory Waldenström's Macroglobulinaemia
pmc-11637722.creator: Jaimal Kothari, Toby Eyre, Ali Rismani, Kushani Ediriwickrema, Darren Edwards, Sevasti Galani, William Wilson, Anthony Lawrie, Laura Clifton‐Hadley, Helen McCarthy, Angela Collins, David Lewis, Suzanne Arulogan, Rebecca Auer, Guy Pratt, Ruth de Tute, Roger Owen, Shirley D'Sa
pmc-11637722.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryThe optimal therapeutic approach for relapsed/refractory (R/R) Waldenström's Macroglobulinaemia (WM) has not been clearly defined, especially after treatment with chemoimmunotherapy (CIT) and covalent Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors (cBTKi). The PembroWM trial is a multi‐centre, phase II, single‐arm study assessing the safety, tolerability and efficacy of rituximab with pembrolizumab in R/R WM patients who had received at least one prior line of treatment, with all having relapsed post‐CIT and most also exposed to cBTKi.

pmc-11688944.title: DESIGNING AND DISSEMINATING AN EDUCATIONAL PROGRAM IN OVER-THE-COUNTER HEARING TECHNOLOGY
pmc-11688944.creator: Yi Shen, Dana Urbanski, Susan Anderson, Adrian Lee
pmc-11688944.description: Over-the-Counter (OTC) hearing aids have been available to the US market since October 2022. These “do-it-yourself” hearing devices were introduced to promote accessibility and affordability of hearing healthcare to primarily older adults with perceived mild-to-moderate hearing loss. To date, many new delivery models of hearing healthcare have emerged in response to the availability of OTC hearing aids.

pmc-12620053.title: Variation in Social Feeding Behaviors and Interactions Among Caenorhabditis Nematodes
pmc-12620053.creator: Dustin Haskell, Jhelaine Palo, Reina F H Eugene, Christopher R L Large, Michael P Hart
pmc-12620053.description: The ability to respond to stimuli and environmental cues is essential for higher order organisms to survive and reproduce and requires a neuronal network that can integrate cues and execute behavioral responses. Evolution of behaviors occurs ubiquitously in most established ecological niches, even among closely related species.

pmc-13049132.title: Direct optimization of the probability of lesion origin in proton treatment planning for low‐grade glioma patients
pmc-13049132.creator: Tim Ortkamp, Habiba Sallem, Semi Harrabi, Martin Frank, Oliver Jäkel, Julia Bauer, Niklas Wahl
pmc-13049132.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). pmc-13134993.title: A case of autoimmune hemolytic anemia with acquired functional mutation of the TLR7
pmc-13134993.creator: Yu Han, Hongbo Chen, Ying Li, Yuhong Yin, Xiuxian Zhu, Xiaoyan Wu
pmc-13134993.description: This article presents a case of recurrent autoimmune hemolytic anemia in a child with a gain-of-function (GOF) mutation of the TLR7. This patient’s condition contrasts with the six previously documented cases of GOF mutations in the TLR7, thereby expanding the phenotypic spectrum of such mutations and enhancing clinical comprehension of childhood systemic lupus erythematosus (cSLE).

pmc-13277405.title: Sludge compost: a double-edged sword for depleted soil restoration revealed by integrated multi-omics analysis
pmc-13277405.creator: Xiaojie Mei, Wenqing Wu, Ning Fang, Yali Guo, Xiaohu Dai
pmc-13277405.description: The prospective use of sludge compost for restoring depleted soils requires balancing its agronomic benefits against potential ecological risks. This study employed an integrated metagenomic and metabolomic approach to evaluate the dose-dependent effects of sludge compost on soil properties, maize growth, and rhizosphere microbial communities.

pmc-13556795.title: 354. Effects of psilocybin treatment on cognitive function in Japanese patients with treatment-resistant depression: an open-label study
pmc-13556795.creator: S Tomiyama, K Yonezawa, K Kusudo, L Harada, M Matsui, K Suzuki, D Stoliker, S Nakajima, H Tani, H Uchida
pmc-13556795.description: BackgroundCognitive dysfunction is associated with impaired psychosocial functioning in patients with major depressive disorder (MDD). Patients with treatment-resistant depression (TRD) exhibit more pronounced cognitive dysfunction than those with non-resistant MDD, underscoring the need for effective therapeutic strategies. Psilocybin has emerged as a promising treatment for depression due to its rapid onset and sustained antidepressant effects.
